# Pending changes (since patch 0019, 2026-11-23)

## 2026-11-23 - Veins in the ground, new controls, diving, the tutorial's rewards, the rocks' faces

Asked: "rocks that contain minerals appear to have flipped faces"; "mining should not just be a rock, sometimes it
should be a mining vein inside the ground - if the dig laser is equipped it can be used to dig the ground to obtain
the minerals, far higher quantity than in a simple rock. When a mining vein is scanned by the scanner I want to see a
ghost image overlayed of the vein itself so I know where to dig exactly"; "E should be a navigation button of
strafing right, use the left click instead, which now is context sensitive: a grab hand cursor for grabbing and
interacting with things. The scanner is now assigned to right click"; "add the ability to swim with a proper
animation"; "the interactive tutorial should have clear rewards per step in drachmas".
Done:
- **The deposits' rocks the right way out** (CosmosDeposits._lump: its triangles wound clockwise seen from outside -
  Godot's front faces; the lumps had shown their insides, lit backwards).
- **Veins** (new CosmosVeins): ore bodies 3-10 m under a world's ground - a winding chain of 4-7 joints of one
  mineral, 70-260 units (a deposit has ~13-30) - found round you a cell (70 m) at a time on a worker, 40% of cells;
  the terrain digger's carves that cut into one put its ore in your pack (4 a carve: "+4 Tin Ore - the vein: 120
  left"); what's left kept in the save (extra veins). The scanner shows the veins within 160 m as glowing ghosts
  through the ground in their mineral's colour for a minute, marked with their depth ("Tin Ore vein (140) - 5 m down").
- **Controls**: E (and Q) strafe - the ship's thrusters, and on foot; the **left click** on foot does what's in reach
  (talk, a terminal, a seat, your pilot's seat, a package) - a grab hand at the crosshair shows it - else it fires;
  the **right click** on foot is the scanner (Z too); G gets you up from the pilot's seat (landed or docked too). The
  prompts say "Click: ..." / G. The free mouse's own buttons never count as clashes in Settings.
- **Diving**: at the surface F / Ctrl dives; under water you swim in three dimensions (3.2 m/s, Shift faster; Space
  up, F / Ctrl down, a slow drift up between), on the sea floor too; back up at swimming depth or in the shallows,
  you float again. The swim / swim_idle / dive / dive_idle clips while you do (the walk ones until they're there).
- **The tutorial's rewards** on a line of their own: "Reward: 50 dr · earned 330 of 3,090 dr".
Files: scripts/world/space/cosmos_veins.gd (new), scripts/world/space/cosmos_deposits.gd,
scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, scripts/world/game/cosmos_sandbox.gd, scripts/world/game/cosmos_tutor.gd,
scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd, scripts/core/keybinds.gd.

## 2026-11-23 - The player swims: surface and underwater clips (Blender)
Asked: swimming with a proper animation.
Done: four new looping clips in external/blender/automaton/moves.py (the automaton's own list; other skins don't
swim), baked and exported to art/player_3d:
- swim - a head-up front crawl: body ~20-30 deg from level, head up looking ahead, arms stroking in turn (a closed
  path through 7 key points per arm, _loop_path), a little roll, a flutter kick (2 kicks a leg a stroke).
- swim_idle - treading water: upright, hands sculling, an egg-beater kick, a slow bob.
- dive - an underwater breaststroke: glide, sweep out, pull, hands under the chin, frog kick, glide.
- dive_idle - hovering underwater: tipped ~50 deg forward, slow sculling and kick.
Water line: the walker's origin SWIM_DEPTH = 1.25 m under the surface (moves.SWIM_LINE): in swim the neck's base is
at 1.34 m, the head's top at 1.62 - head, neck, shoulder tops out. The head tips back at most ~38 deg (past ~44 the
helmet meets the back armour); every frame checked for parts through each other.
Numbers: swim 42 frames (1.4 s), swim_idle 60 (2.0 s), dive 48 (1.6 s), dive_idle 60 (2.0 s), 30 fps; the player
model 44 clips (was 40).
Files: external/blender/automaton/moves.py, automaton.blend; art/player_3d/player.glb + model.json.

## 2026-11-23 - Under the sea: the underwater look and the sea's life
Asked: "add an underwater shader as well as underwater ecosystem with creatures, plants and rocks".
Done: CosmosUnderwater (scripts/world/life/cosmos_underwater.gd), a node Cosmos adds: while the camera's under a
water sea, two full-screen passes from the depth buffer (no screen copy - it alone cost ~0.7 ms): pass 1 multiplies
- the water's absorption per colour along each ray and on the sunlight's way down (red first, darker deeper) and
the caustics on what faces up; pass 2 adds - the water's own scattered light, light shafts (3 dithered steps), and
the surface from below: Snell's window with the sun's glare and a bright rim, total internal reflection outside it,
rippling. Drifting specks round the camera (600, one draw). The air's shells hidden under the sea. The life round
you: kelp forests, sea-grass meadows, branching/boulder/fan corals, barrel sponges, urchins, boulders - from the
planet's seed and palette, scattered by 24 m cells (each its own seed, built on a worker, every kind of all cells
one MultiMesh), by depth and in patches, to 60 m, streamed as you swim, drawn only under the surface, swaying in a
turning current. Animals: 4 fish schools (3 species), 2 rays, an eel/sea serpent, a bloom of glowing jellyfish -
moved in the vertex shader, the script steering each group (keeps to the water, wanders round you, schools and rays
bolt). Warmed at the title (CosmosWarm). A new fps tour scenario "under the sea".
Hooked in (cosmos.gd): the node in _build; diving, the camera goes under the sea with you (kept above the floor,
not the surface); the floor's boulders and corals solid to a swimmer or diver (walker_bumps).
Numbers: ~18 draws; ~1100 floor things round a dive spot (kelp 229, sea grass 429, rocks 278...); cells 24 m, 123
in reach, built in 20 ms on a worker; script 40-47 us a frame under water; floor life + passes ~0.27 ms a frame
(quiet estimate); fish 190 tris, ray 466, eel 480, jelly 280.
Files: scripts/world/life/cosmos_underwater.gd (new), shaders/world/underwater.gdshader, underwater_glow.gdshader,

## 2026-11-23 - The worlds orbit their star in the game; the solar map shows the world you're on
Asked: "the solar system seems to not display the planet I am currently on, I don't need to explore the whole planet
for it to appear in the solar system map as long as I am on it it should be enough; make sure that the orbits of
planets and moons are correctly displayed on the map and that they correctly move around both inside the map and in
the game in general".
Found: in the game the worlds were placed once, when you came into a system, and never moved; the map away from the
game worked their places out on the galaxy's clock - the two drifted apart. The solar map's fog was swept round your
ship only - on foot with no ship (a new game) nothing was ever revealed, not even the world under you.
Done:
- One orbit code for the game and the maps (Cosmos.orbit_period / orbit_angle / orbit_point / orbit_pos_at /
  planet_places / co_orbit / system_places): each world round its star on Galaxy.time (period 3600 s x (orbit /
  30 km)^1.5), each moon round its world (960 s), the orbits' tilts the records' own.
- In the game the worlds really move (Cosmos._orbit_tick, every frame): stations, asteroid fields and lairs within
  a world's orbit band (15 km, or its moons' reach) co-orbit it, keeping their place from it (clear of its air and its
  moons' orbits) - so no world ever sweeps through one; further out they stay put. Whatever is within a moving body's
  reach (a world: 5 radii, 6-20 km; a station: its reach + 2.5 km; a field; a lair) is carried with it by as much as
  it moved - you on its ground, your ship (and a landing under way), the camera, other ships, creatures, a monster's
  home ground - by the body whose surface is nearest of those whose reach holds it (on a world's ground, that world - a
  moon overhead must not carry you: it did, and you were thrown about the ground near a moon); towns, pirate camps
  and cave / dungeon entrances are children of their world now (they move with it, nothing to carry - a town near
  a moon had been carried off with the moon, 3.8 km above its world, while the map showed it where it belonged); who rides which body looked at again 24 a frame, newcomers at once.
- The solar map: in the game it shows the bodies where they are now (4 times a second); away from it (Talos) the
  same places from system_places. Orbits drawn in each world's own colour (told apart from the grid's rings), moons'
  round their worlds. "You" is you on foot (not your ship). The world you're on or flying low over is always shown;
  worlds your sensors pass near are known from then on (Galaxy.planets_known, saved) wherever their orbits take
  them; the sensors sweep the fog round you on foot too.
- Guide: the solar map's worlds move.
- Tests: test_worlds_orbit_and_carry_you (a minute on: the world where its orbit says, you where you stood on its
  ground, moons round their worlds, stations co-orbiting and the map's places the game's, the world you're on known);
  test_orbits_clear_of_stations_and_fields (every system, 24 times over 11.8 hours: nothing ever in a world's path).
Numbers: a world at 43 km orbits at ~44 m/s (period 1.7 h), a moon ~47 m/s round its world; 120 systems x 24 moments
checked clear; carry: 24 riders re-looked a frame.
Files: scripts/world/space/cosmos.gd, scripts/ui/pages/map_page.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_map_mirror.gd,
scripts/sim/galaxy.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd, tests/test_maps.gd, data/docs/game.md.

(span: half the view's height on the ground); the camera rides over the ground under the view and below 3% of the
radius narrows its view instead of going lower. Over a town you've walked into the camera keeps closing in on it
while the plan (the same worker-drawn texture, now mipmapped) fades in over the globe, laid exactly where the town

to all there at that zoom - buildings first, then the place names, then you and your ship (the globe's marks fade
out), the dark ground, title, north arrow and scale last. Fully in, the plan's own zoom carries on (spare wheel
notches kept); zooming out hands back to the globe and fades back. A click on the town or "Town plan" plays the same
zoom as a 0.7 s eased dive; Back / Home reverses it. Unvisited towns: the globe stops at its nearest. Also: dragging
near the ground moves the ground with the cursor, keys turn slower close up, a double click turns to a mark.

## 2026-11-23 - Vein ghosts on the ground only; dug veins show their ore
Asked: "the mining vein overlay should overlay over the ground not anything else, right it overlays even over the
automaton, also veins should be colored differently when they are excavated with the digger tool".
Done:
- The scanner's vein ghost is no longer meshes drawn over everything (no depth test): the ground itself draws it.
  CosmosVeins._send passes the veins round you to the planet's terrain shader as uniforms - up to 16 veins / 112
  points (planet-local chains, radius, span, bound, colour, what's left, metal / glow / crystal), the shown ones
  first (ghost_n), the ghost's strength (ghost_k). Each bit of ground glows in the mineral's colour over the vein
  nearest it across the ground: a filled body, a sharp outline, a faint halo, fainter the deeper it lies, a slow
  pulse along it. The automaton, plants, boulders, ships, buildings - and the HUD - hide it. 60 s, fading over the
  last 6.
- Dug veins: the carved ground's chunks (CosmosVoxels, instance uniform `voxel`) show solid ore inside a vein's
  radius (ragged edge) - the mineral's colour banded and seamed, smoother, a sun highlight tinted by the metal
  (white glints for crystals), its own glow if it has one. In the ghost the parts dug into go grey and each vein dims
  with what's left - both already saved. Mined-out veins kept (0 units) so their pits still show ore.
- Found on the way: int uniform arrays reached the GPU scrambled (spans are float vec4s); the ore colours are sRGB
  (converted to linear in the shader).
- Test: test_veins_scanned_and_dug - the ghost is the terrain's, no no-depth-test meshes, it fades, the dug vein's
  "left" reaches the shader. Doc shot space3d_vein retaken; the guide's Digging paragraph.
Numbers: 16 veins / 112 points of uniforms; same window and view: old shader 467-470 fps, new with nothing shown
459-464 (~0.02 ms), ghost shown (2 veins) 440-442 (+0.1 ms, for its minute only). Glow out to 2.6 x the vein's
radius, 0.3 x as bright at 11 m down.
Files: shaders/world/terrain.gdshader, scripts/world/space/cosmos_veins.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_voxels.gd,
scripts/world/models/cosmos_warm.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd, tests/doc_shots.gd, data/docs/shots.json,
data/docs/game.md, data/docs/shots/*.jpg.
- (orbits, frame rate) The worlds step on 30 times a second (everything near a body moves with it in the same step:
  a world's 1.5 m a step unseen) and each orbit's tilt is drawn once - the orbits' cost a frame 0.36 ms -> ~0.02 ms;
  on foot among plants and animals 420 -> 655 fps (same machine, same load).

## 2026-11-23 - Characters: your own parts and clips layered over the generated ones
Asked: a workflow to improve the generated Blender assets by hand - replace parts, replace whole assets, or add
(new animations, improved ones) - starting with changing the automaton's head.
Done:
- external/blender_overrides/ (README.md, overrides.py): one `<skin>_overrides.blend` a character - a Reference
  (the generated rig "Rig", its parts as gen:Head, gen:Torso, ..., its 44 clips as gen:<clip> actions, refreshed
  from the generated .blend by a script) and the user's Overrides collection. Made for the automaton
  (automaton_overrides.blend), starting with a copy of the generated head as "Head" to change; two scripts in its
  Text editor: refresh_reference, export_to_game (saves, exports, runs Godot's import).

  replace or add clips (length from the action, loop / gun from its properties or the clip it replaces). Problems
  reported (a part on no bone, vertex groups that aren't bones, a gap at a join, a material new to the game) and
  written with what was taken into model.json "overrides". `overrides.py <skin> check` shows it without exporting.
- tests/test_overrides.gd: every exported character's overrides without problems, its added clips in the model.
- Tested end to end on a scratch copy: a taller head, a crest added on the head bone, a new clip -> exported
  (Head replaced, Head_Crest added, wave added, 0 problems), rendered beside the generated one.

## 2026-11-23 - The local pilot boards his ship and flies it
Asked: "the npc has not boarded the ship and he does not walk to his captain chair to sit before taking off".
Done:

  its hull, in its own space (carried as the world turns), to the ramp's foot - up the ramp (from there a child of
  its insides, no longer one of the town's people), along the middle of its deck through its doorways, round the
  pilot's seat's left side and across into it, turning to the consoles, the "sit" clip; seated he's carried with the
  ship wherever it flies (a hired ride's field, a station's pad) and leaves with it. If you board first he runs.

  goes back to his town; no pilot at all, it flies as before.

  passenger seat beside it. A local pilot's ship is always the small trader (CosmosNpcShip.setup hull_as) - a
  200 m hauler's bridge was a minute's walk away.

  waits there, a new one once it climbs. The pilot's "my ship's on the field" line only from that ride's own pilot.
- The guide's "Making a living": the local pilot's ride.

trader; the step into the seat 0.8 s; lift-off waits at most 60 s; seated: only his clip posed.

## 2026-11-23 - The maps open on you; the solar map fluid

Asked: "all maps should always auto focus at first on the player", "movement in solar map is stop motion like i want
it to be fluid".
Done:
- Every map opens centred on you - each time it's shown (its sub-tab, M, G, the 1-4 keys), not only the first time
  (MapsPage.show_sub -> each map's focus_you, at once, no easing); you pan and zoom freely after, reopening centres
  again. The planet map: the world you're on (or nearest), the globe turned to your spot (as Find yourself, any town
  plan closed; out in space, the side facing your ship); a world picked on the solar map stays picked. The solar map:
  on you - or the world you're on (on foot or landed); the first time in a system at the whole system's zoom, after
  that the zoom you left. The galaxy map: your system, at the zoom you left (1300 the first time).
- Why the solar map stepped: what's where was gathered four times a second (rebuild every 0.25 s), the markers and
  names over the picture drawn 8 times a second while the view rested; while panning / zooming the 3D picture was
  made every frame but the overlay at most 60 times a second (the markers lagging the picture), and the stems,
  foot circles and the sensor ring only remade at those gatherings (their size jumping while zooming).
- Now: everything that moves placed again every frame the screen shows (Map3DView.frame_hz: the screen's refresh
  rate, 60-240) to the galaxy's clock - Cosmos.place_now: a world (or what co-orbits it) worked out from Galaxy.time,
  what rides one (you, your ship) moved on by its body's motion since the last 30 Hz orbit step - the overlay drawn
  with every picture; the gathering (who's known, ships in sensor range, the panel) still four times a second.
  Moving: the picture and the overlay made together at the screen's rate (no longer the 3D picture 600 times a
  second, the overlay 60).
- Cheap: the stems and the circles at their feet are two MultiMeshes of one line mesh each (a stem, a unit circle),
  the sensor ring one circle mesh, all placed by transforms - building those lines anew each frame was 1.5 ms, now
  placing everything that moves is ~0.12 ms; the overlay ~0.3 ms (headless).
- The solar map page takes the 3D game from the menu (world) when given (else the current scene, as before).
Numbers: placing a frame 1.5 ms -> 0.12 ms; positions 4 Hz -> the screen's rate; overlay at rest 8 Hz -> every frame
shown.

## 2026-11-23 - The flight HUD redrawn: a compass bar on top, the sights in the middle (VEL, ALT)
Asked: the user drew the HUD they want (a curved compass strip on top - its heading boxed under it; in the middle a
crosshair, rings and tick ladders, a target box and the distance, a curved VEL gauge left and ALT right with their
values in pointed boxes) - "this is for flying the spaceship; use the compass also when I am on foot. Remove any
redundant GUI element that used to display the same info". Then: "the spaceship should draw on top of the circular
hud, also make the circular hud half its current size"; "the compass should display markers with the things already
detected".
Done (scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd, all procedural - arcs, lines, polygons, glow as two wider faint strokes):
- The compass bar, top centre, in the ship and on foot: an arched band of dark glass, its ends hooked up, letters
  every 45° (N in red), ticks every 5°, 135° either side; the notch, the heading boxed on its lower edge. Heading
  convention (compass_frame / bearing): near a world (6 radii; on foot always) up is away from its centre and north
  its pole (+Y - worlds don't spin; latitude is measured the same way) laid on the level, east = north x up (east =
  the way longitude grows); out in space the system's plane: north -Z, east +X. Facing: the ship's nose; on foot the
  camera's. Hidden inside a ship, a hangar, below ground, docked.
- Its marks: what's already known at its bearing - the HUD's markers' bodies (worlds and the star a disc, stations a
  diamond, gates an hourglass, ships and monsters a triangle, towns a square) and on foot the scanner's finds
  (squares, their colours); hostile red, the target ringed with its distance under the bar, an arrow at the bar's end
  when it's past it; 40 at most, looked up 10 times a second (the bearings change only as you move), all drawn as one
  batch of triangles.
- The sights (flying): a ring of 0.15 x the screen's height - the crosshair, the glass band, the outer ring bright in
  four arcs, thin rings, a dotted one, tick ladders left and right, the diamond in its circle and the target box's
  corners; the distance to the target (or to the ground the nose points at); the stick's mark; VEL (speed, log scale
  to the Hyperion drive's top) and ALT (height over the nearest world's ground, its sphere far off; log scale to
  100,000 km; the world named under it) on curved glowing bars in glass housings, their values in boxes pointed
  outward on the crosshair's line. The centre stays exactly at the screen's middle (where the shots meet).
- The ship over the sights: its meshes also on render layer 19, drawn alone each frame by a camera that sees only
  them (a SubViewport at half the screen's size, transparent, matched to the game camera in frame_pre_draw); the
  sights' canvas shader (shaders/hud_ship_mask.gdshader) leaves them out where that mask covers - 0.13 ms GPU,
  0.1 ms CPU measured (a 60 Hz window), only while the sights show. Warmed at the title (CosmosWarm._text).
- Cheap: the fixed lines (bands, rings, ladders, housings, boxes) drawn once into layers of their own (redrawn when
  the screen's size changes); each redraw (60 Hz) only the moving parts: ~190-240 us headless (compass with marks +
  sights), 80-120 us the compass alone on foot.
- Removed as now shown by these: the compass ring round the health gauge and its heading number, the speed number
  and the speed arc under it (VEL), the "Nearest: X (kind) N km" / "Altitude N over X" line (ALT). The readout keeps
  the drive's state (FLIGHT / BOOST / HYPERION, the well), the throttle bar, latitude / longitude, heat, the guns.
- The 2D HUD's messages moved down under the compass bar (hud.tscn Message: top 128, was 72).
Docs: game.md (the interface line, the compass bar, the sights, the readout), tutorial.md (the readout step, the
stick's ring); shots retaken (17), space3d's notes rewritten (readout, compass bar, health, VEL, ALT, stick),

## 2026-11-23 - Atrapos Sans: the game's own typeface, everywhere; text never under 12 px
Asked: design the main font from the user's reference sheet (a wide, extended, geometric squared sans) and use it
everywhere; then (feedback) give every letter enough space to read; then (standing rule) no text under 12 px.
Done:
- tools/make_font.py builds "Atrapos Sans" from code (fontTools): every glyph is put together from primitives -
  rounded-rectangle rings with superellipse corners (n 2.6), stems, slanted strokes with horizontal cuts, chevrons -
  combined by union / difference / intersection in a small boolean engine of its own (edges split where they cross,
  the boundary pieces kept, chained into clean contours: no overlaps, outer contours clockwise). Two weights from the
  same drawings: Regular (stem 96 units) and Bold (114). Units per em 1000, cap height 680, x-height 470, ascenders
  690, descenders 200, line 930 + 270. Single-storey a and g, flat-apex A, tabular figures, curly quotes.
- 319 glyphs a weight: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, the ASCII punctuation, Latin-1 (accented letters, ß Æ Œ Ø Þ Ð, ° ± × ÷ µ

  tubes along smooth curves through its points, as thick as it is there, under a wireframe cage (a ring at each of

  break between (radius -1), the radius eased along each segment (its vein_pts 112 -> 384); digging finds them all;

  (CosmosBuilds.push_body from CosmosCreature / CosmosNpc) and push an unlocked shut door open - never a locked one.

  record, in the save). It shows past each quarter (wear 1-3: COLOR.a now packs paint + 9 x wear; the building shader
  darkens it with soot and draws cracks - Voronoi edges - wider and more of them); only then is its chunk rebuilt.

## 2026-11-23 - Swimming keeps stroking; no sky through a fresh dig
Asked: "swimming animation stops while swimming in water, excavating ground reveals sky for a while instead of just ground".
- Swimming: the walker set only idle/walk/run (and their gun versions) to loop, so swim, swim_idle, dive, dive_idle, carry and carry_idle played once and froze. Now every clip model.json marks `loop` loops (cosmos_walker.gd _ready). Test: test_swimming_and_diving checks the clips loop.
- Digging: a carve was sent to the terrain shader at once (the ground there undrawn) while the voxel chunks that draw the dug ground were still building on workers - the sky showed through the hole for a few frames. Now a carve waits in CosmosPlanet._cuts_wait until CosmosVoxels.ready_at says the chunks round it are built (2 s at most), then goes to the shader (cuts_settle, called each frame by the voxels); the old ground stays drawn till then. Test: test_veins_scanned_and_dug checks the wait and the send.
Files: scripts/world/player/cosmos_walker.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_planet.gd, scripts/world/space/cosmos_voxels.gd, tests/test_cosmos.gd.
- The guide's digging picture (space3d_digging): the planet's info window no longer over it (the target cleared before the shot), and the dig spot kept 70 m from your ship (its hull was at the picture's edge). Retaken. File: tests/doc_shots.gd.

## 2026-11-23 - Free building (a sandbox switch)
Asked: "playtest the building system with no restrictions". Added BuildKit.free_build (the user arg --free-build): nothing costs anything (placing, upgrading), nothing needs holding up and nothing falls when a piece is taken away, towns are no bar; sockets and overlaps still count. The HUD's build panel and the build menu say "Free building". Test: test_build.test_free_building.
Files: scripts/world/build/build_kit.gd, build_plan.gd, cosmos_builds.gd, scripts/ui/build_menu.gd, scripts/world/player/cosmos_hud.gd, tests/test_build.gd.

## 2026-11-23 - The builder's preview steady
Asked: "the building cursor in the building mode flickers and moves all over the place randomly". Snapping judged each socket by its distance to where the line of sight first hit something - a point that jumps metres as the sights slide off a face's edge (a near wall, then the ground behind) - and offered the sockets already filled, so the preview sat on pieces already there. Now (BuildPlan.snap with the camera's ray): sockets judged by how near the line of sight they are (smooth with the mouse), taken ones passed over, the one shown kept unless another is 0.5 m clearly nearer. Test: test_build.test_snapping_by_line_of_sight.
Files: scripts/world/build/build_plan.gd, scripts/world/build/cosmos_builds.gd, tests/test_build.gd.
- Still flickered: the real cause. The previews (children of Cosmos, the scene's root) were put in place with the aim, 30 times a second, while the planet under them moves every frame (measured in play: 1.8 m every few frames) - so each preview drifted up to ~2 m off and jumped back. Now each keeps its planet-local place ("on" meta) and CosmosBuilds._ride puts it back on its world every frame (measured: 0.0 m off). File: scripts/world/build/cosmos_builds.gd.

## 2026-11-23 - Click and drag places runs again
Asked: "click and drag for placing multiple pieces does not seem to work".
- On open ground (the first foundations of a new structure) the preview made a new frame round the aim every update - its grid moved with you, so the drag's end was always the start's cell: a run of one. Now the frame where the drag began is kept while you drag (_drag_frame) and the aim's cell is read on its grid.
- The run's pieces on a new structure are checked on the real ground (the drag frame's), not a flat guess.
- Free building: the run no longer counted materials (each piece you couldn't afford showed red).
- Test: test_build.test_drag_a_run_on_open_ground (a 3 x 2 run placed into one structure).
- The guide's building shot: its setup stood you 6 m aside, so one foundation fell outside the builder's reach and the porch's columns went on the wrong piece; you now stand in the plot while it's built, and the triangle's found by type. Retaken.
Files: scripts/world/build/cosmos_builds.gd, tests/test_build.gd, tests/doc_shots.gd.
- Still red in play: the run's own town check didn't heed free building (one piece's did) - building in a town, every piece of a run was refused. Fixed; the drag test now drags a run in a town too (fits with free building, refused without).
